assessments.reasoning: The commit-pinned LLVM LICENSE.TXT, capture b29149afb46941e6a729129783c9594c, contains the base instrument and the exception in sequence. The heading and paragraph at bytes [11611,12493) distinguish the two named licenses and their roles.

The SPDX detail at the release target, capture 03957e2fe484429f8a35f65626d3054b, explicitly says the exception was created for Apache-2.0. Its exception text preserves the separate GPLv2 condition. It supplies context for the publisher’s base designation.

challenge.method: Tested GPLv2 and the adjacent University of Illinois/NCSA legacy license as alternative bases. Checked whether mentioning §§3 and 9 automatically waives those sections.
challenge.results: The heading expressly selects Apache 2.0. GPLv2 supplies the conditions against which a court must find conflict, and the legacy license has its own later heading. Sections 3 and 9 are examples of potentially conflicting provisions. The election also covers another section found to conflict, always in its entirety and solely for the Combined Software.

limitations: This verifies the named base edition in the publisher document. Application to any file, court decision or actual software combination requires separate evidence.
reasoning: The project banner, the January 2004 Apache License Version 2.0 text and the inline exception heading all identify Apache-2.0 as the base. The second paragraph introduces GPLv2 as the license of the software combined with compiled LLVM forms. Its references to the patent and indemnity provisions resolve to §§3 and 9 of the preceding Apache text.
